Severe and chronic diarrhea is accompanied by dehydration 
and electrolyte depletion. If also accompanied by prolonged 
infectious, immunodeficiency, or inflammatory disease, malab-
sorption of vitamins, minerals, and protein or fat also may 
occur, and nutrients may have to be replaced parenterally or 
enterally. In some forms of infectious diarrhea, loss of iron 
from GI bleeding may be severe enough to cause anemia. Nutri-
ent deficiencies themselves cause mucosal changes such as de-
creased villi height and reduced enzyme secretion, further con-
tributing to malabsorption. As the diarrhea begins to resolve, 
the addition of more normal amounts of fiber to the diet may 
help to restore normal mucosal function, increase electrolyte 
and water absorption, and increase the firmness of the stool.
